title: DORA | Capabilities: Trunk-based development
summary: DORA capability page: trunk-based development (few branches, daily merges, no freezes) correlates with delivery performance; heavy async review and untested commits are pitfalls.

assertions.quote: teams achieve higher levels of software delivery and operational performance (delivery speed, stability, and availability) if they follow these practices
large merges frequently introduce bugs or regressions
it is hard to reason about the impact of large changes on a system through inspection, defects are likely to escape the attention of reviewers
When code review is laborious and takes hours or days, developers avoid working in small batches
If your team practices pair programming, then the code has already been reviewed by a second person.
The longer a merge is delayed, the more likely it is to create merge conflicts and associated issues.

verdicts.note: The delay-to-conflict link is well supported; whether synchronous review is practical at scale is less clear.

assertions.quote: it's essential that tests are run against code changes before commit

verdicts.note: Standard CI mechanism; effectiveness depends on suite coverage and speed.

DORA states that for CI to be impactful every commit should trigger a successful build and test run, and finds CI predicts continuous delivery; whether this keeps trunk releasable is implied rather than measured.

assertions.quote: Many developers simply can't imagine working in this way.

verdicts.note: Adoption reports consistently cite resistance; the magnitude is anecdotal.
